spots.name: Wairere Falls
spots.coordinates_source: OSM trailhead car park (Wairere Falls Track); falls at -37.734, 175.88
spots.reason: Falls are in the Waikato district near Matamata. Straight-line they are 27 km from Tauranga and 52 km from Hamilton, both at the edge of those spans, but across the Kaimai ridge (about an hour's drive from either) and neither city is the base for them. Visitors come from Matamata, Tauranga and Hamilton, so no one base owns it: standalone. FLAG for the Waikato pass.
spots.bio: A 153 m waterfall in the Kaimai Range, reached by a DOC walking track.
spots.note: Region overlap with Waikato; check the Waikato pass has not also placed it. Two counted sources (Wikivoyage, DOC).

new_destinations.name: Waihi
new_destinations.case: Wikivoyage chapters for Waihi and Waihi Beach; the beach, the Orokawa walk and the Karangahake Gorge (Hauraki Rail Trail, Te Aroha nearby) give three kept spots in a 20 km cluster outside the Tauranga and Coromandel spans. Waihi town centre coordinates are approximate and need a source.
new_destinations.status: proposal only, needs description, reasons with photos, tips, best months, header. Straddles Bay of Plenty and Waikato: coordinate with the Waikato pass.

new_destination_note: Waihi is the only proposal; its three spots are placed standalone with proposed_destination set so none is lost if declined. Papamoa, Kaiate Falls, Maketū and Katikati Bird Gardens fit Tauranga's 30 km (75%) span with no span change. Wairere Falls is standalone (Waikato side of the Kaimai, no single base). No other cluster is thick enough (Ōpōtiki + Motu Trail are two).

existing_fixes.note: Run python3 scripts/curation/bio-fit.py --text on it. Check the photo is not the museum interior or a pre-2000 view (Rotorua shipped with a 1913 view before).
